findings.issue_text: Sibling-host check collapses unrelated public-suffix domains such as evil.co.uk and forum.co.uk to co.uk, incorrectly displaying an external site path as same-domain
Hostname comparisons are case-sensitive, so URLs with uppercase hostnames such as https://EXAMPLE.com/user fail to match example.com and incorrectly omit their path

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sibling-host check collapses unrelated public-suffix domains such as evil.co.uk and forum.co.uk to co.uk, incorrectly displaying an external site path as same-domain

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real bug in the website_name method. The code at lines 142-144 checks if two hosts have the same number of domain parts and more than 2 parts, then compares everything after the first part. For domains like 'evil.co.uk' and 'forum.co.uk', both have 3 parts, so the code compares 'co.uk' == 'co.uk' which is true, causing it to incorrectly treat evil.co.uk as a same-domain site and display the full path. This is a security/correctness issue where unrelated domains sharing a public suffix would be treated as related.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hostname comparisons are case-sensitive, so URLs with uppercase hostnames such as https://EXAMPLE.com/user fail to match example.com and incorrectly omit their path

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. In the `website_name` method in `user_serializer.rb`, the code compares hostnames using `==` and `ends_with?` operations (e.g., `website_host == discourse_host`, `discourse_host.ends_with?(".".concat(website_host))`). These string comparisons are case-sensitive in Ruby. If a user enters a URL like 'https://EXAMPLE.com/user', `URI().host` returns 'EXAMPLE.com' (preserving case), which would not match 'example.com' in the comparisons, causing the path to be incorrectly omitted. The code should use `downcase` on the hostnames before comparison.
